name: Marly’s Mail
author: marlysplugin

sections.description:
A website sends e-mail from everywhere: WordPress for passwords, WooCommerce for orders, plugins for the rest. Each one writes its own. Your customer therefore receives three different-looking letters from the same service, and the only thing deciding which is the plugin that wrote the message.

The flaw is not cosmetic, it is structural. As long as every function composes its own e-mail, every new feature starts from scratch and the logo is forgotten half the time. Marly’s Mail closes the back door: everything that leaves goes through the same frame.

What you set, once

Your logo, the button colour, the background, the text colours and the footer. That’s the whole configuration.

Built for real mail clients

Tables rather than flexbox, because Outlook uses the Word engine. Inline styles, because Gmail strips the style tag on mobile. 600 pixels wide, the only width that passes everywhere. A button that is a coloured cell containing a link, because a real button is not clickable in an e-mail. None of this is a matter of taste — it is what mail clients impose.

WooCommerce

Order e-mails keep their content and receive your header, your footer and your colours. They are not wrapped inside a second frame.

See it before your customers do

A preview opens the result in your browser, and a test send puts it in the inbox where it will really be read.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin and activate it.
  2. Open Settings → Marly’s Mail.
  3. Set your logo and your colours, then send yourself a test.
sections.faq:
Will it break e-mails from my other plugins?

No. A message that already carries a full HTML page — WooCommerce order e-mails, for instance — is left alone and only receives your header and footer.

My logo does not appear

Use a PNG rather than a WebP: Outlook 2016 to 2021 cannot read WebP and shows a cross instead. The address must also be in HTTPS, which the plugin enforces.

Does it send the e-mails itself?

No. It dresses them; your server or your SMTP plugin still sends them.
